newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: SAVINGS BANK'S LOAN RESTRICTIONS LIFTED.
newsitem.headline: SAVINGS BANK'S LOAN RESTRICTIONS LIFTED.

text.p: Lithuania's central bank said on Thursday that it had lifted the loan restrictions on the huge state-run Savings Bank.

"The board of the Bank of Lithuania decided today that Savings Bank's financial report on April 1 showed that it was meeting all of the risk limiting requirements of the central bank," the central bank's spokeswoman told Reuters.
The bank was stripped of the right to issue loans in the summer of 1995.
In November of 1996, the restrictions were partly lifted and the bank was allowed to lend money provided no single loan exceeded five percent of its capital.
All restrictions have now been lifted on the bank, which is the only one of the three big state banks not slated for privatisation.
"Lately, the biggest sum we could lend to a single client was around 3.5 million litas," the head of Savings Bank's credit department, Vidmantas Bukinas, told Reuters.
The bank reported a profit of 30 million litas in 1996 after posting losses of 39 million litas in 1995.
